summary: The root فَهِمَ (fahima) means to understand or apprehend something with the mind. It implies grasping the meaning of something, similar to knowing or perceiving with the heart.
lane: 1 فَهِمَهُ ذ , aor. فَهَمَ , inf. n. فَهْمٌ (S, Msb, K, &c.) and فَهَمٌ , (Msb, K,) which is the more chaste, (K,) but the former is a dial. var. [more] extensively obtaining, or, as some say, it is a subst. used as an inf. n., (Msb,) and فَهَامِيَةٌ (S, K) and فَهَامَةٌ and فِهَامَةٌ , (K,) He understood it, or knew it with the mind; he apprehended its meaning; syn. عَقَلَهُ , (JK,) and عَلِمَهُ (S, Msb, K) and عَرَفَهُ بِالقَلْبِ . (K.) And فَهِمَ عَنْهُ [ He understood what he (another) said ]. (A in art. خرس ; &c.) [See also فَهْمٌ below.] -b2- فَهُمَ , meaning He was, or became, such as is termed فَهِيم [i. e. one having much understanding ], is like عَلُمَ , meaning “ he was, or became, such as is termed عَلِيم . ” (TA.)
